title: Noor and the Spire
premise: Wren Eastwick has spent fifteen years hiding a forbidden gift: the ability to steal and store memories as charms, selling them quietly in Grayhollow, a city where magic is outlawed. When a mute child named Noor arrives at Wren's door speaking a language older than any kingdom, Wren discovers the child carries half of an ancient covenant binding the human realm to the Spire — a living tower whose slow death is unraveling both worlds. Hunted by the Wardens who enforce the ban and betrayed by the fence who once protected them, Wren must choose between erasing their own stolen past to power the covenant or keeping the identity they built from other people's memories. In the end, Wren gives up every charm they own — including the memory of their true name — to reforge the covenant with Noor as its new keeper, finding belonging not in what they remember but in what they willingly release.
about_author: Ansel Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one claimed, which explains a lifelong obsession with things people leave behind. They write fantasy about outsiders who keep the world running without ever being allowed to belong to it.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. A routine night of selling memory charms in Grayhollow's night market goes wrong when a Warden patrol nearly catches Wren mid-trade. We learn how Wren steals memories, why magic is banned, and that Wren keeps one charm they will never sell: a fragment of their own forgotten childhood. Emotional beat: wary loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Wrong Hour
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. A child appears at Wren's garret door at dawn, mute except for words in a language no one alive should speak. The child, Noor, carries a cracked stone seal that hums when touched. When Wren accidentally reads Noor's memories, they see the Spire dying in dreams. Emotional beat: reluctant wonder; Wren cannot turn the child away.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Burn
chapters.summary: POV: Wren, shifting briefly to Warden-Captain Ilsa Vane. Vane raids the night market hunting a 'resonance' traced to Wren's street. Wren hides Noor among the charms, realizing the child's presence endangers everyone who ever bought a memory. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve — Wren decides to run rather than let others pay.

chapters.title: The Fence Who Knew Too Much
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Wren seeks help from Corvane, the fence who has shielded them for fifteen years, only to discover Corvane has been reporting to the Wardens all along — he knows what Wren truly is. Betrayed, Wren flees with Noor through the city's drowned underlevels. Emotional beat: the collapse of the only family Wren had.

chapters.title: Noor Speaks
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Inside the underlevels, Noor finally finds words in Wren's presence, explaining in broken common tongue that the Spire was the covenant's anchor and it chose Noor as its last speaker. Noor reveals the seal needs a second bearer willing to give up something irreplaceable. Emotional beat: trust kindled between two people with no pasts they can claim.

chapters.title: The Archive of Stolen Names
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Following Noor's instinct, they reach a hidden archive where outlaws hoard confiscated magic — including records of Wren's original theft fifteen years ago. Wren learns their stolen childhood memory belongs to someone else entirely, and their whole identity is a patchwork. Emotional beat: identity crisis; who is Wren if the memories were never theirs?

chapters.title: Vane's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV: Ilsa Vane. Cornering Wren and Noor, Vane offers a deal: surrender the child and walk free. But Vane privately doubts the ban she enforces — her own sister was erased by it. She gives Wren until moonset. Emotional beat: the antagonist revealed as a prisoner of the same law, complicating Wren's hatred.

chapters.title: Ascent to the Hollow Crown
chapters.summary: POV: Wren and Noor alternating. Evading Vane's cordon, the pair climb the dead Spire itself, passing shrines of forgotten keepers. At the summit, the covenant's broken heart demands its price: a life's worth of memory, freely given. Wren understands what must be surrendered. Emotional beat: dread transfigured into acceptance.

chapters.title: The Giving
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. At the Spire's crown, Wren pours every charm — every stolen memory, every purchased identity — into the covenant while Noor sings the old language to bind it. Vane, arriving too late to stop them, chooses instead to hold off her own Wardens. The Spire breathes again. Emotional beat: climax; grief and liberation in a single act.

chapters.title: A Name With No Owner
chapters.summary: POV: Noor, closing on Wren. Memoryless but unbroken, Wren wakes in Grayhollow as a stranger — yet Noor remembers for both of them, and the city's outlaws shelter the pair who saved the covenant. Magic remains illegal, but now there are two keepers watching the border between realms. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; belonging found not in a name, but in being chosen.
